**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Strip lab metadata from unauthorized projections**

At reviewed head `5d8d71083db3f4f949ddd91a0b2f3f83ff19bdea`, when privacy, lock/fullscreen, or the selected role makes `allowed(a)` false, `publicItem()` masks the visible fields but still shallow-spreads this newly attached `labRef`. Consequently both `clinical:activity` and later snapshots disclose the stable report ID and `abnormalCount` to a client that failed authorization; omit `labRef` from the masked projection rather than relying on the UI not to render it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 57ac3036cb82fd096bc98ba8b015aedb48afbc76. publicItem omits labRef from masked copies without mutating the source. Six regression cases cover privacy, lock, fullscreen and three unauthorized roles across snapshots and activity broadcasts; all six failed before the fix and now pass.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use a monotonic clock for the report lifetime**

At reviewed head `5d8d71083db3f4f949ddd91a0b2f3f83ff19bdea`, the elapsed budget is driven by `Date.now()`, so moving the system clock backward while an unpaused report is open stops elapsed time from accruing until wall time catches up. The Rust deadline protects only `nativeIsland`; browser and native-studio previews can therefore retain the report well beyond the intended 60-second lifetime. Base the budget on a monotonic source such as `performance.now()` while keeping wall-clock values out of elapsed-duration calculations.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 57ac3036cb82fd096bc98ba8b015aedb48afbc76. Every report-budget call site now uses performance.now(), including native deadline synchronization and visibility resume. The browser Hook test reproduces a one-hour system-clock rollback and now clears within the monotonic lifetime; three repeated runs pass after repairing the test pauseAt scheduling margin.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid focusing the island merely to enable capture protection**

At reviewed head `5d8d71083db3f4f949ddd91a0b2f3f83ff19bdea`, `active` does not prove that the user clicked the island: a `clinical:view` broadcast enters the summary at `controller.ts:72`, calls `load()`, and invokes this command. The unconditional `set_focus()` then steals the foreground from the studio or the application where the user was typing; capture affinity should be applied without activation, with focusing reserved for a separately proven direct island click.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L14-L14](https://github.com/peterkis/light-island/blob/7f9947a8e0b7e8d3d3deb045197f1599b9583f59/AGENTS.md#L14-L14)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 57ac3036cb82fd096bc98ba8b015aedb48afbc76. Capture protection no longer invokes set_focus; explicit user/source-window activation remains separate. A bounded native test verifies the actual Win32 foreground stays on the studio through the clinical:view broadcast. The pre-fix baseline also retained foreground on this machine, so the evidence does not claim a reproduced OS focus theft.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Invalidate ticket-backed reports when revisions change**

At reviewed head `57ac3036cb82fd096bc98ba8b015aedb48afbc76`, when a full report is displayed in the standalone `?source=` window, `request.current` is null because that window never initiated `clinical:open`. A later `clinical:activity` for the same object with a newer version or withdrawal therefore bypasses the request-key cleanup, while the report stored here continues rendering obsolete full rows indefinitely; invalidate `source` and `sourceLabReport` against subsequent activity/snapshot identity and version changes in ticket-backed windows too.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L63-L63](https://github.com/peterkis/light-island/blob/57ac3036cb82fd096bc98ba8b015aedb48afbc76/AGENTS.md#L63-L63)
